source.note: Original explanatory adaptation. The 35-day and 30% baselines come from the assignment, not measured software results. The order, reference mismatch, queues and customer dialogue are illustrative. No individual team's waiting time is claimed.

scenes.title:
Connected country.
Disconnected order.
scenes.label: TURKISH MARKET CONTEXT / NOT A PERFORMANCE COMPARISON

beats.text: A business orders a connection. Then waits thirty-five days for service.
Turkcell, Türk Telekom and Vodafone are familiar names. This story follows a fictional operator, not those companies.

scenes.title:
One order.
Five separate worlds.
scenes.label: CUSTOMER RECORDS > ORDER DESK > AVAILABLE CAPACITY > FIELD TEAMS > PARTNERS

beats.text: One business order passes through customer records, the order desk, capacity checks, field teams and partners.
Each step means passing the details to someone else.

scenes.title:
Copy. Paste.
Check. Repeat.
scenes.label: EXAMPLE OF A COPIED NUMBER / NOT A RECORDED INCIDENT

beats.text: Staff type the same details again. Imagine one order number copied incorrectly.
Someone must check the mistake, correct it and type it again. The customer is still waiting.

scenes.title:
The order travels.
Staff pass it along.
scenes.label: TURKIYE / SERVICE PARTNERS IN THE BALKANS AND CAUCASUS

beats.text: Partners across the Balkans and Caucasus cannot exchange order details directly with the operator's systems.
Staff must pass information along. More chasing. Less clarity about progress.

scenes.title:
Not forward.
Back around.
scenes.label: 30% NEED REWORK / CASE-STUDY FIGURE / NOT NECESSARILY LOST ORDERS

beats.text: The case study says thirty percent of orders get stuck and need more work.
The same work comes back, while new orders keep arriving.

scenes.title:
A signature today.
Service weeks away.
scenes.label: 35 DAYS FROM ORDER TO SERVICE / NO WAIT TIMES ARE ASSIGNED TO TEAMS

beats.text: Thirty-five days from order to working service. Five weeks before the customer can get started.
That is the overall delay, not a measured wait for any individual team.

scenes.title:
Where is my order?
When can we start?
scenes.label: EXAMPLE CUSTOMER QUESTIONS / DELAYS RISK LOSING CUSTOMERS

beats.text: The customer wants service quickly and clear progress updates. Instead, questions pile up.
Delays put business relationships at risk. Waiting becomes a reason to leave.

scenes.title:
Demand accelerates.
Manual work cannot.
scenes.label: GROWING BUSINESS DEMAND / ILLUSTRATIVE QUEUE, NOT MEASURED VOLUME

beats.text: Demand for business connections and online services is growing faster than staff can handle by hand.
Partners are choosing providers that make exchanging orders easier. Repeated work makes it harder to compete.

scenes.title:
Orders pile up.
Business is at risk.
scenes.label: TODAY'S CHALLENGES ONLY / NO PROPOSED SOLUTION

beats.text: Thirty-five days to start service. Thirty percent of orders need more work. Customers wait.
Customer trust is at risk. Revenue waits. Competitors do not.
